mcqs.question: A student measures the length of a table three times and records 120 cm, 122 cm and 119 cm. Another student measures the same table three times and records 121 cm, 121 cm and 121 cm. Which set of measurements is more reliable?

options.D: It cannot be decided without more information

mcqs.explanation: The second set shows no variation; repeated measurements that are the same indicate low random error and therefore higher reliability. The first set varies by 3 cm, showing larger random error. Hence option B is most reliable.

mcqs.question: A child estimates the length of a pencil to be 15 cm. Using a ruler, the actual measured length is 13 cm. Which statement best compares the measured and estimated values?

options.A: The estimate is 2 cm longer than the measurement.
options.B: The estimate is 2 cm shorter than the measurement.
options.C: The measurement is 2 cm longer than the estimate.

mcqs.answer: The estimate is 2 cm longer than the measurement.
mcqs.explanation: The estimated value (15 cm) exceeds the measured value (13 cm) by 2 cm, so the estimate is longer. Option A correctly describes this difference; the other options state the opposite or claim equality, which are incorrect.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes the difference between measurement and estimation?

options.A: Measurement is an exact value obtained using an instrument, while estimation is an approximate value made without an instrument.
options.B: Measurement is always larger than estimation.
options.C: Estimation uses a ruler, whereas measurement relies on guessing.
options.D: Both measurement and estimation give the same level of precision.

mcqs.answer: Measurement is an exact value obtained using an instrument, while estimation is an approximate value made without an instrument.
mcqs.explanation: Measurements involve tools (ruler, scale) that give a specific value, whereas estimations are educated guesses without precise tools. Options B, C, and D are misconceptions.

mcqs.question: Which of the following actions will most improve the accuracy of a length measurement?

options.A: Using a ruler that has finer scale markings
options.B: Measuring the object as quickly as possible
options.C: Using a longer ruler even if it has coarse markings

mcqs.answer: Using a ruler that has finer scale markings
mcqs.explanation: Finer scale markings allow the observer to read the measurement more precisely, reducing systematic error. Speed, length of the ruler, and poor lighting do not improve accuracy and may increase error.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an example of a systematic error?

options.A: A ruler that is incorrectly marked 1 cm longer than the true length
options.B: Applying different amounts of pressure each time a spring balance is used
options.C: Slightly different readings each time because of hand shaking
options.D: Changes in ambient temperature that cause the object to expand

mcqs.answer: A ruler that is incorrectly marked 1 cm longer than the true length
mcqs.explanation: Systematic errors are consistent and repeatable, such as a mis‑calibrated ruler that always adds 1 cm. Options B and C describe random errors, and D is an environmental factor that can cause systematic or random effects but is not a clear calibration error like A.

mcqs.question: A student measures the length of a book three times: 20.1 cm, 20.3 cm and 20.2 cm. What is the best single estimate of the book’s length?
mcqs.explanation: The average of the three readings is (20.1 + 20.3 + 20.2)/3 = 20.2 cm. Using the mean of repeated measurements gives the most reliable estimate, so option B is correct.

mcqs.question: A student estimates the distance between two desks as 30 cm. The actual measured distance is 28 cm. Which statement correctly describes the estimation?

options.A: The estimate is within 2 cm of the measurement, showing a good estimation.
options.B: The estimate is off by 2 cm, indicating a poor estimation.
options.C: The estimate is exactly the same as the measurement.
options.D: The estimate is larger than the measurement by 10 cm.

mcqs.answer: The estimate is within 2 cm of the measurement, showing a good estimation.
mcqs.explanation: Being only 2 cm away from the true value means the estimate is close and therefore good. Option B incorrectly labels a 2 cm difference as poor, while C and D are factually wrong.

mcqs.question: When planning a garden, Maya needs to know the length of a fence. She guesses it to be about 5 m because she has no measuring tape. Later she uses a tape and finds it is 4.8 m. What does this scenario illustrate?

options.A: Measurement provides an exact value, while estimation gives an approximate value.
options.B: Estimation is always more accurate than measurement.
options.C: Both methods give the same level of precision.
options.D: The fence length cannot be known without a ruler.

mcqs.answer: Measurement provides an exact value, while estimation gives an approximate value.
mcqs.explanation: Maya’s initial guess is an estimation—an approximate value. The tape measurement gives a precise, exact value (4.8 m). This contrast is captured in option A. Options B, C, and D misrepresent the nature of estimation and measurement.
